newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -Gilts losing steam, face 115-05 barrier.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -Gilts losing steam, face 115-05 barrier.

text.p: September gilt futures are losing momentum and must crack resistance at the 115-05 contract high on Tuesday to avoid a correction, technical analysts said.
"Gilts seem to be running out of steam, there's no great willingness to take on 115-02/05," said Marc Ostwald, technical analyst at London Bond Broking.
"If we're going to get further we need to test those levels today otherwise we're in for a set back."
The market failed at 115-02 on Monday, after hitting 115-05 last Wednesday.
By 0704 GMT, September gilts were down 2/32 at 114-24.
Ostwald put initial support around 114-17 to 114-19. Charts show the market hit a low of 114-17 on Monday, a high of 114-18 on June 30 and a high of 114-19 on June 27.
"Below there, we're looking to 114-02/05 which is an area of congestion around some old highs," said Ostwald.
The market hit a high of 114-02 on June 26 and 114-04 on June 25.
"There's no buying power on the upside, there's not much willingness to get into the long end of the market," said Ostwald. "It needs to correct a bit...to a level where the buyers will come in."
Juliette Clark, senior treasury manager at the Royal Bank of Scotland, agreed the time was not yet right for a swing higher.
"Range trading is therefore expected today, although the underlying bull bias should remain present," she said in a note for clients.
Clark said trade would oscillate around 114-26, with resistance at 114-30 and support at 114-20. Below there, congestion support at 114-17/18 comes in.
"If that manages to halt the slide then the bulls will remain on course for gains this month," she said. But a break lower will open a move to 114-11/13.
Ostwald said congestion from October 1993 around 115-17/18 would act as a barrier.
By 0733 GMT, December short sterling was unchanged at 92.65.
